recipes.name: Stewed Cabbage
ingredients_raw: 1 medium head cabbage, cut into squares
1 (14.5 ounce) can stewed tomatoes, with liquid

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion, celery, and garlic and saute for 3 to 5 minutes, or until translucent. Stir in cabbage, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Pour in tomatoes and season with salt and pepper to taste. Cover pan and cook over medium heat for 30 to 40 minutes, or until cabbage is tender.

raw_recipe.headline: Stewed Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: Classic dish of cabbage stewed with tomatoes, celery, onions and garlic.

review.reviewBody: Everyone enjoyed this recipe as a great side dish! I modified it to make it a bit healthier by cooking the onions, celery, and garlic in 1/4 cup vegetable broth, instead of the butter, and it came out great. Thanks for a quick and easy addition to any meal!

I've made this recipe multiple times with some slight variations: (1) If I didn't have the canned tomatoes (or even if I did), I made this in my fry pan with bacon fat or salt pork fat instead of butter, sliced kielbasa, and if I needed other "liquid", I added a bit of apple cider or balsamic vinegar for a nice burst of flavor. I didn't need rice, as I am diabetic, and this needed to be as keto as I could get it. (2) I have also done this up (using ground meat). It is a recipe from my late cousin Ann, who called it "Unstuffed Cabbage Rolls" (see photo for recipe). (3) Using your original recipe, for a little heat, add some red pepper chili flakes or spicy bbq rub or curry (or all three).

I always use a 28-oz can of tomatoes, and instead of salt I season with VEGETA seasoning (It's a Croatian seasoning that we love. You can find it on Amazon.) Sometimes I will brown some sliced frankfurters with the onions and celery, and add some water to make it more of a cabbage soup.
Many folks will add sausage. Yet, we add Italian seasonings (basil, oregano), then plate it with tortellini or ravioli on top.

This is a good guide. Weights and sizes are helpful. A “medium” cabbage is vague. I cut my 3 pound cabbage in half. 1 1/2 pounds was enough. My large saucepan was too full to stir, so transferred to 5 qt. Dutch oven. Of course the cabbage gets smaller as it loses water, but the larger pot made for easy stirring. Served with grilled sausages and roasted red potatoes. Thanks !

Delicious and easy! I used extra butter and first fried up some Polish sausage in the butter, then added the onion and celery (extra celery). I also put it all in the slow cooker and cooked it that way after first frying the sausages and onions celery and garlic. I also added at least a teaspoon or two of cilantro.

This recipe surprised me- in a good way! I could not believe how such an easy recipe with so few ingredients could end up making something so truly delicious. I followed it exactly-but because we wanted to enjoy it as a main course- added some smoked beef sausage-(cut up)as the cabbage simmered-and because I love tomatoe-added a bit more as well.. I did also add apprx 1 tbsp sugar as it simmered because I like a tad bit of sweetness- but wow- how good it ended up because the sausage lent just the right amount of smokey flavoring- to balance it out to one big- YUM! Thank you so much for posting. I will definitely make this again.

If you like cabbage and you like tomatoes, you'll like this dish. I had some cabbage to use up in the fridge and was lucky enough to have a can of no salt added diced tomatoes with italian seasonings in the cupboard. I used more garlic and celery than listed and put in veggie broth instead of butter. Turned out great! I had to cook it a lot longer than the recipe called for, closer to 1.5 hours. And I took the advice of another poster and added a can of drained kidney beans. Perfect dish for a nutritarian such as myself as well as my husband who enjoys eating vegetarian every other day. Thanks for the simple, healthy, delicious recipe! :)

I will definitely make this recipe again! All of the ingredients were right here on hand in my kitchen. I used the advice of an earlier reviewer and added ground sausage to the onions an celery, cooked them together, added minced garlic, cabbage, and then a can of whole roma peeled tomatoes and juice. I also added a tablespoon of pesto, a tablespoon of hidden valley ranch seasoning, and salt/pepper. It was great!

Very good recipe. I added a little water, because I wasn't sure there was enough liquid for the 40 minutes I steamed the cabbage. I didn't leave anything out but added some smoked paprika and some cumin and dried thyme (all in moderation). 
It turned out really well, and my almost teenaged daughter liked it served with rice.
used fresh tomatoes and added quinoa to soak up juice. served with parmesan cheese.
Great flavors! I didn't have celery, but will use it next time. I added a little ground fennel seed and served it over polenta and sliced ham. Very adaptable recipe.
Didn't have celery so added thyme, think I'll add a splash of pickle juice next time 😋

I get a lot of cabbage always looking for new ways to prepare it. I didn't have stewed tomatoes in my pantry but I had a can of fire roasted crushed tomatoes 🍅. On a cold day with toasted sourdough bread toast this dish hit the spot.
Was exactly what I was craving! I didn’t change the recipe, except to throw some sliced kielbasa in about 15 minutes before it was ready. This will definitely be in our cold weather rotation!
This was great. I just had a third of a cabbage leftover so I halved everything but the celery and can of tomatoes. Turned out great. Thinking it will be great with leftover Polish sausage also.

What's the shelf life of this in the fridge after cooking? Also I changed the recipe. Double the stewed tomatoes ( 28 oz total) added a few blocks of frozen spinach ,added 2 cans of Chicpeas rinsed ... Also took others advice, I added some onion powder, chilli flakes, oregano.. made for a really great and easy complete meal with lots of leftovers for meal prep! Simple , heaty, and delicious!!

The base here is great- add some depth of flavors….red pepper flakes, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano 🌿 cayenne pepper chili powder dried basil. A shallot or two also helps. EVOO instead of butter.
Simple ingredients. Easy to make. Make ahead and warm when needed. Stores great, so make the whole recipe and enjoy the leftovers later in the week

Loved this! I was skeptical because I don't usually add tomatoes. I did tweak a little but. I uses crushed tomatoes because I don't like big pieces of tomatoes in certain things. I also added vegetable broth instead of all of the butter as one reviewer here did, and I added a tbsp of white vinegar. This was amazing!
